answer: To keep a flood of fake agents from capturing rewards, require every newcomer to take a slow, public path onto the network. Picture a stone jetty where only established peers may walk a candidate in after its stake has sat untouched through one full checkpoint. Mass-created wallets snag on a reef of unspendable locks and delayed countersignatures; cloning a wallet does not clone that waiting time. If a later vote looks too similar to an earlier one, the chain keeps an echo of the first signer set, and the copies add no weight until they pay the same cost.
